sources.title: Yuantong Temple - The Oldest Buddhist Temple in Kunming - ChinaXianTour
sources.content:
Yuantong Temple in Kunming - Complete Information

Overview
Yuantong Temple, situated on Yuantong Street in central Kunming, is described as "the oldest Buddhist temple in Kunming" with over 1200 years of history. It functions as the largest temple in the city and uniquely integrates three major Buddhist traditions: Mahayana, Theravada, and Tibetan Buddhism.

Historical Background
The temple was originally constructed "during the Nanzhao period of the Tang Dynasty (around 766 AD)" under the name Butara Temple. In 1301, during the Yuan Dynasty's Dade reign, it received its current name Yuantong Temple, referencing one of Guanyin Bodhisattva's titles. The Ming Dynasty witnessed expansions including the Jieyin Hall. During the Qing Dynasty in 1688, significant reconstruction occurred under Wu Sangui's patronage.

Architectural Highlights

Inverted Slope Temple Design: The unusual layout descends rather than ascends, with terrain becoming progressively lower as visitors venture inward, culminating at the Yuantong Hall.

Yuantong Hall: The central main hall houses "sitting statue of three Buddhas" carved during Emperor Guangxu's reign. Notable features include "two columns with a height of more than 10 meters" carved with colored dragons and "five hundred Arhat" sculptures on walls.

Water Courtyard: The temple features a distinctive "Free Life Pond" surrounded by connecting corridors, creating a "water pavilion style" temple.

Cultural Integration
The temple demonstrates rare integration of multiple traditions, including a "Bronze Buddha Hall" representing Theravada Buddhism and Thai-style architecture housing a Buddha statue gifted by Thailand. Taoist influences appear in decorative elements throughout the complex.

Visitor Information
- Address: 30 Yuantong Street, Wuhua District, Kunming
- Entrance Fee: RMB 6 (includes complimentary candles and incense)
- Operating Hours: 08:00-17:00
- Recommended Duration: Approximately 2 hours

Transportation
Multiple bus routes serve the temple (85, 92, 95, 100, 101, 119, 187, 235, Z5). Subway Line 6 to Tangzixiang, transfer to Line 2, exit at Chuanxin Gulou Station, then walk westward approximately 1100 meters.

Nearby Attractions
- Kunming Zoo (Yuantong Mountain Zoo)
- Green Lake Park
- Nanping Pedestrian Street

sources.title: Kunming Must See - The Yuantong Temple | WindhorseTour
sources.content:
Kunming Must See - The Yuantong Temple

Yuantong Temple is located at the foot of Yuantong Hill in the northern part of Kunming and, with a history of more than 1,200 years, is one of the grandest as well as the most important Buddhist temples in Yunnan Province.

King Yimouxun of the Nanzhao Kingdom built it during the late eighth century as a continuation of Putuoluo Temple. It is not only the largest temple in Kunming, but also a religious holy site that integrates the three major sects of Mahayana Buddhism, Theravada Buddhism, and Tibetan Buddhism (Lamaism).

One of the most distinctive features is its layout: Unlike all other Buddhist temples, which are built on an ascendant, you enter Yuantong Temple from above and descend along a gently sloping garden path.

The temple complex is built around Yuantong Hall (Mahavira Hall), which is known as the Fane on the Water for it is surrounded by a very large pond filled with limpid water and fish. A delicate stone bridge which has an elegant octagonal pavilion stands in the center connects Mahavira Hall and the Yuantong Temple entrance.

In 1982, Thai Buddhists sent a copper statue of Sakymuni to Yuantong Temple as a symbol of friendship, and the statue is three and a half meters high and four tons in weight. A few years later, in 1985, a Copper Buddha Hall was built in a combination of Chinese and Tai styles to house this exquisite gift.

Entrance Fee: CNY 6
Opening Hours: 08:00-18:00
Recommended Visit Duration: One or two hours

Take Metro Line 2 to Chuanxingulou and walk west for about 15 minutes.

sources.title: Yuantong Temple: Largest Buddhist Temple in Kunming - Top China Travel
sources.content:
Yuantong Temple: Largest Buddhist Temple in Kunming

Yuantong Temple, built in the late Tang Dynasty, is the largest and oldest Buddhist temple in Kunming with over 1,200 years of history. Located at the foot of Yuantong Hill in central Kunming, it is easily accessible and serves as an active religious site.

The temple uniquely combines Mahayana, Theravada, and Tibetan Buddhist traditions under one roof. Its distinctive downhill layout is the opposite of most Chinese temples.

Key features include the octagonal pavilion in the central pond, the main Yuantong Hall with its dragon-wrapped columns, and the Copper Buddha Hall built in Thai-Chinese fusion style.

Every spring, the temple grounds and nearby Yuantong Hill are covered in cherry blossoms, making it a popular destination for both worshippers and nature lovers.

Kunming Yuantong Temple Travel Guide

Yuantong Temple is the largest and most famous Buddhist temple in Kunming, with a history spanning over 1,200 years. Located at the foot of Yuantong Hill in central Kunming, the temple is known for its unique inverted slope design and integration of multiple Buddhist traditions.

The temple complex features beautiful gardens, a central pond with an octagonal pavilion, and several halls housing important Buddhist statues and artifacts.

Visitor Information:

- Hours: 08:00-17:00
- Duration: 1-2 hours
- Transportation: Metro Line 2, multiple bus routes

The temple is particularly beautiful during spring when cherry blossoms bloom on Yuantong Hill.

sources.title: 圆通禅寺 - 百度百科
sources.content:
圆通禅寺（昆明）完整信息

基本信息
圆通禅寺位于云南省昆明市圆通街，始建于公元八世纪（唐朝南诏时期），是昆明市最大的佛教活动场所。

历史沿革
该寺院建于唐南诏蒙氏时期（738～902年）。南诏王阿儿罗凤之子异牟寻为治理蛟龙之患而创建，初名"补陀罗寺"。后因战火毁坏，仅留荒址。

元大德五年（1301年），云南行中书省左丞阿昔思主持重建，历时19年至元延七年（1320年）完成，改名为"圆通寺"。

明清两代继续修葺扩建。康熙七年（1668年），吴三桂大规模扩建，建造了"圆通胜境"牌坊和八角亭等。1949年后经多次重修，1977年国家拨款翻修大殿，1983年移交佛教协会管理。1998年被公布为省级文物保护单位。

建筑与结构特色
山门与前厅：进入山门后可见"圆通胜境"坊，前厅供奉一尊二米高的纯铜释迦太子说法像。
水池与八角亭：池中央有清康熙年间建的八角亭，亭内供奉千手观音，四周石廊环绕，南北石桥相连。
大雄宝殿：建筑面积600余平方米，为重檐歇山式宫殿。殿内供奉三身佛（法身毗庐遮那佛、应身释迦牟尼佛、报身），配以元代塑造的十二圆觉像和护法诸天。殿中两根高15米的圆柱上有青赤二龙蟠绕，为明代工匠艺术结晶。
铜佛殿：建于1985年，融合中国、泰国、印度建筑风格。内有一丈多高的释迦牟尼铜身坐像。

宗教特色
圆通寺是"中国最早的观世音菩萨道场之一"。后殿塑像中央为观世音菩萨（云南十方丛林中罕见的男性观音像），左为文殊菩萨，右为普贤菩萨。

摩崖石刻与文化遗产
寺院周围保存大量摩崖题刻，包括南诏异牟寻元封元年刻的摩崖大"寿"字、明代李元阳草书诗文、清代多位官员与书法家的题刻与诗作。

现状
现任住持淳法法师。寺院为国务院确定的汉族地区全国重点寺院，每年三月樱花盛开吸引众多游客。

sources.title: Yuantong Temple, Kunming Travel Information & Guide
sources.content:
Yuantong Temple, Kunming Travel Information & Guide

Yuantong Temple is a renowned Buddhist temple located at the foot of Yuantong Hill in central Kunming. With a history of over 1,200 years, it is the largest and most important Buddhist temple in Yunnan Province.

The temple is notable for its unique downhill architecture, its integration of three Buddhist traditions (Mahayana, Theravada, and Tibetan), and its beautiful garden setting with a central pond and octagonal pavilion.

Along with the patronage of the local people of Kunming and Yunnan in general, Buddhists from around the world come here on pilgrimages to pay homage. There are special Buddhist services two times each month, and the Buddhist Association of Yunnan Province is located here.

The temple is free to visit for worshippers and charges a nominal CNY 6 entrance fee for tourists. It is easily accessible by public transportation from anywhere in Kunming.
